# SK2031 — Do not discard a setter's value parameter

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A property, indexer or init accessor body does work and never mentions `value`, so every assignment through it is discarded while appearing to succeed.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Syntax |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |
| ReSharper | `ValueParameterNotUsed` (`resharper_value_parameter_not_used_highlighting`) |

## Why

The setter's whole contract is to consume `value`. One that runs statements and never reads it stores something else, or stores nothing, and the caller has no way to see that the write went nowhere. The repair is a decision about what the setter was meant to store, so the rule reports and does not rewrite.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
public int Retries { get => retries; set => retries = DefaultRetries; }
```

Write:

```csharp
public int Retries { get => retries; set => retries = value; }
```

## When it does not fire

Only accessors with a body are examined; auto-properties, abstract, extern, interface and partial declarations have none. Three shapes earn an exemption because the discard is legible as deliberate rather than accidental: a body with no statements at all (`set { }`), a body that only throws, and an accessor or member carrying `[Obsolete]`. That is the line: an empty setter announces that it ignores the write, and a setter that does work while ignoring it does not. `value` counts as read wherever it is mentioned in the body, including inside a lambda, a local function, a nested accessor and `nameof(value)` — the last is conservative on purpose, since a name mentioned is a name the author had in mind. Statements the file's preprocessor directives disable are not in the body, so a setter emptied by `#if` reads as the empty exemption. The rule does not judge whether the value stored is the right one, only whether one was read.

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2031.severity`
